chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Harun ibn Harizah, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was in prostration (sujood), and he had lifted his two feet from the ground, with one foot resting on the other. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It is permissible that he (peace be upon him) did this out of necessity, because the more preferable act is what we presented earlier, which is placing the two thumbs on the ground.
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for placing the feet during prostration in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility in the physical execution of *sujood*, illustrating the principle that the Imam’s actions often accommodate practical necessities while maintaining ritual validity. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan’s commentary clarifies the hierarchy of practices, distinguishing between the permissible act of lifting the feet and the more preferred *sunnah* of placing the thumbs on the ground, thereby resolving apparent discrepancies in juristic reports. This reflects the Shia scholarly approach of balancing strict adherence to prophetic tradition with pragmatic adaptability in worship.
